title: Training Meets the Track: Meyer Takes 2026 Service School to Pocono Raceway
body_markdown:
For Meyer dealer technicians, the day offered a chance to get practical knowledge, connect with fellow dealers and experience one of the most recognizable racing venues in the country.


And with Meyer celebrating its 100th anniversary, it was a fitting setting for a company built on a century of innovation and dealer support.


Learning by doing: Technicians work directly with Meyer hydraulic systems during interactive classroom sessions.


### **From Classroom to Truck Side**


Led by Meyer Service School pioneer Lou Orazem, the technical training explored the evolution of Meyer’s hydraulic systems, with a focus on Lot Pro, SuperV-3, and Super Blade hydraulic units.


Technicians reviewed electrical and hydraulic systems, truck-side mount installation, plow assembly and setup, maintenance, troubleshooting, and service best practices.


After 16 years leading Meyer Service Schools, Lou has seen firsthand how both the products and the training have evolved.


“I remember when presentations were delivered using three slide-projector reels, and the occasional jam was part of the agenda.” he recalls. “Today, the training is much more direct and interactive, especially with the addition of 14 new hydraulic units over the past 27 years.”


Technicians put their training into practice, attaching and detaching the Meyer Blaster with the Quick-Hitch attachment system.


Outside, dealer technicians got an opportunity to work directly with Meyer equipment, including demonstrations of the ProMount Attachment System and the Blaster with Quick-Hitch Attachment System.


The Blaster Quick-Hitch generated excitement, with attendees impressed by how easily one person can attach and the[spreader](https://www.aebi-schmidt.com/en/products-solutions/products/spreaders/) from the truck.


For technicians, that kind of participatory training can translate directly to the work they do every day, helping them diagnose issues, complete installations, and answer customer questions with greater confidence.


“During breaks, technicians exchanged questions, shared stories, and solutions. Attendees were collaborating, answering one another's technical questions before Lou even had to step in,” notes Jason Mattson of Meyer Customer Service. “Well-trained technicians can help deliver faster installations, reduce callbacks and give end users a better experience with Meyer products.”


Attendees step outside the classroom for a behind-the-scenes experience at Pocono Raceway.


### **Extracurricular Activities**


Starrlee Warner, Manager of Track Operations at Pocono Raceway, gave attendees a behind-the-scenes tour that included the Media Center, a look at the history of the track, and a visit to the Pit Garage.


Inside the garage, technicians got an up-close look at approximately 12 NASCAR race cars, two jet drying trucks, and around 15 go-karts, offering a unique glimpse into the equipment and operations that keep a major racing facility running.


The experience provided a memorable break from the technical training while giving attendees the opportunity to connect and explore the facility. Combined with a full day of technical training and time spent with fellow technicians, the Pocono Service School proved to be a successful day of learning, connection, and a little racing-inspired fun.


Meyer looks forward to creating more opportunities like this at future Service Schools, bringing technical training to unique locations, and giving technicians an experience worth remembering.


The Meyer Demo plow stands ready outside Pocono Raceway, marking a memorable day of training, connection, and real-world learning.


### **Continuing the Legacy of Dealer-Focused Support**


For 100 years, Meyer has been evolving with the needs of the people who use, sell, install and service its products. While the details of the training have changed throughout the years, the goal has remained the same:


**Give Meyer dealers the knowledge, confidence and support they deserve.**


Whether you are new to Meyer or have years of technical experience, Service School is an opportunity to sharpen your skills, learn directly from Technical Service, and gain valuable insight from fellow dealers and technicians in the field. It’s a chance to share real-world experiences, exchange ideas, and connect with the people behind the products.
